19717844.reason: RE-LY major bleeding, dabigatran 150 mg vs warfarin, from the FDA PRADAXA label (October 2010) Table 2: 399 (3.3) vs 421 (3.6), HR 0.93 (0.81, 1.07), randomised patients 6076 vs 6022. The effect tuple equals the NEJM 2009 Table 3 original's, but the counts differ (375 vs 397 there): an identical effect never establishes an identical version. Version chain PENDING (see docs/source_versions.json).

supersedes.source: RE-LY (PMID 19717844) abstract, approved-dose harm row: 'The rate of major bleeding was 3.36% per year in the warfarin group, as compared with ... 3.11% per year in the group receiving 150 mg of dabigatran (P=0.31).' Source-reported dose-specific RR 0.93 (95% CI 0.81 to 1.07) is the 150 mg major-bleeding effect named in the HM lane audit; used to recover the registered harm without changing the efficacy dose rule.

21830957.safety_population: on-treatment safety population (on treatment plus 2 days): 7111 rivaroxaban vs 7125 warfarin
21830957.reason: ROCKET-AF major bleeding from the FDA XARELTO label Table 5: 395 (3.6) vs 386 (3.5), HR 1.04 (0.90, 1.20), ON TREATMENT PLUS 2 DAYS (safety population, 7111 vs 7125). Distinct from the article's principal safety composite, major and non-major clinically relevant bleeding, HR 1.03 (0.96-1.11), which is not this outcome.

supersedes.source: ROCKET-AF (PMID 21830957) abstract: 'Major and nonmajor clinically relevant bleeding occurred in 1475 patients in the rivaroxaban group (14.9% per year) and in 1449 in the warfarin group (14.5% per year) (hazard ratio, 1.03; 95% CI, 0.96 to 1.11; P=0.44) ... There was no significant between-group difference in the risk of major bleeding'. Source-reported major-bleeding HR 1.04 (95% CI 0.90 to 1.20) is the audit-named harm row; used to recover the registered major-bleeding harm.
